title: The Day the Tablet Slept
subtitle: A funny bedtime read-aloud about a box rocket, a dog named Biscuit and one very sleepy tablet

One interior file serves both: 32 single pages = title page, copyright page (ISBN box), dedication (founder writes it), 24 story pages (12 full-bleed spreads), morning/'The End' page, 'Talk about it' page for grown-ups, 'Plan your own Play Day' page with QR code to the free bonus, 'A note from the author' (founder writes it), endpaper pattern. short_description: Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So Ada and Biscuit the dog build, splash, blast off in a box rocket and bake. A funny bedtime read-aloud for ages 3–7.
long_description:
Shhh… the tablet is sleeping. So what shall we do?

On Saturday morning, Ada zooms downstairs to find the family tablet snoring a teeny-tiny zzz-bip under a purple nightcap. It's taking a day off. So Ada and her dog Biscuit make their own fun. They build a block tower (CRASH!), splash through every puddle (SPLOOOSH, all over Papa's shoes), turn a big empty box into the ADA-1 rocket and blast off past a planet made entirely of socks. Then it's pancakes with Papa, a quiet trip to the library and a growly bear story at bedtime.

Children love to join in on the refrain, shout Biscuit's WOOF!, and spot the sleepy tablet on every page. Short, rhythmic read-aloud pages and bold, full-bleed pictures make it a cozy bedtime book and a fun one to read again and again. The tablet is never the bad guy. It just needed a nap, and in the morning Ada can't wait to tell it about her day.

At the back, grown-ups get 'Talk about it' questions, a 'Plan your own Play Day' page and a QR code for a free printable planner and coloring pages.

For ages 3–7. Pairs with 100 Screen-Free Plays as the Play Day bundle.

launch_notes: Positioning: sell it as a funny bedtime and play-day story, not a screen-time book. Lead with Ada, Biscuit, the box rocket and the refrain in every listing, pin and ad. DEMAND-CHECK.md rates the category Weak and says not to count on this book alone, so its main job is to be the story half of the Play Day bundle. The hardcover file is ready, but per DEMAND-CHECK.md, turn on the IngramSpark hardcover only after the paperback shows sales. Printing costs nothing to hold, but the hardcover needs its own ISBN and a proof.
compliance_notes: No health or medical claims. The book is a story plus parent-education prompts and claims to treat, prevent or diagnose nothing. It is not presented as written by a speech-language pathologist. No autism or diagnosis terms anywhere in the book, listing or keywords. No research citations. No trademarked program names: the grown-up tips use plain words (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one word, follow their lead). No real brands, logos, devices, apps, schools or products: the tablet is a generic, unbranded character, and the copyright page says it is not based on any real product. Zero shame, zero preaching: every spread was checked. The tablet is never a villain or a warning. It takes a day off, the story never says screens are bad, and in the morning the tablet is welcomed back ('Wait till I tell you about my day…'). The 'Talk about it' questions are about rest, play, cooking and Biscuit, not about screen rules. Child safety: puddle play (with Papa), cooking (Papa handles the pan) and box-building are shown with a grown-up nearby, and the copyright page says they are best with a grown-up close by. No balloons, cords or choking-hazard foods appear. The copyright line follows legal/ENTITY.md: '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' The final logo from brand/logo/ is used on the copyright page, the author-note page and the back cover. Print notes: the PDFs are RGB. Chromium embeds the brand fonts as Type 3 fonts. KDP normally accepts both, but IngramSpark prefers PDF/X-1a in CMYK, so run its preflight and convert if it asks [VERIFY]. Check every file against the printer's current template before upload (KDP cover calculator, IngramSpark Cover Template Generator). KDP may print a manufacturing mark on the last page (page 32 is a pattern page, so nothing important is covered) [VERIFY]. Picture books for ages 3–7 are generally treated as ordinary books under US CPSIA [VERIFY with the printer and CPSC guidance].

AI DISCLOSURE (honest answer for KDP): KDP asks whether the book has AI-generated text, images or translations. As built, the story text was drafted with AI (Claude) and the illustrations were drawn by AI-written code. Answer YES for AI-generated images, and YES for AI-generated text unless you have rewritten the text yourself. KDP counts AI-drafted text you later edited as AI-generated; only your own writing that you polished with AI counts as 'AI-assisted', which needs no disclosure. Give the same honest answer if IngramSpark or any store asks [VERIFY each platform's current wording]. If you register the copyright, claim only your own words and your selection and arrangement, and exclude the AI-generated material (see legal/protection/PROTECTION-PLAN.md).

ISBNs: buy your own ISBNs from Bowker (a block of 10 covers this and future books) so AlphaPlay LLC is listed as the publisher. The paperback and hardcover each need their own ISBN. A free KDP ISBN cannot be used at IngramSpark. Paste them into WORDS.md (## isbn-paperback, ## isbn-hardcover) so they print on the copyright page. Let KDP and IngramSpark place the barcode in the labelled 2 x 1.2 in box on the back cover, or place your own there.
